chapter_title: Chương 304: 0306 [Sơn Thôn Lão Thi là phim hài]

segments.title: Chương 304: 0306 [Sơn Thôn Lão Thi là phim hài]
segments.content:
"This 'Crucian Carp with Scallions' is a dish my maternal grandfather taught me to make during the New Year," Bian Guanyue said with pride. "To make this dish, I even brought a jar of pickled peppers and pickled ginger to the capital."

Chen Guiliang took a bite. "Delicious."

Bian Guanyue also tried a bite and said with confusion, "Why does the flavor seem a bit off? It's not bad, but I feel like it's missing something compared to my grandpa's."

Chen Guiliang, who couldn't even tell the difference when listening to vinyl records, was able to identify the problem with the dish after just one bite.

He commented, "You only used red Sichuan peppercorns, not green ones. Also, you used ordinary millet peppers, not the Qixing peppers, which are far superior in aroma and spiciness. The core producing region for Qixing peppers is Longdu and its surrounding cities and counties. You might not even be able to buy them in Rongcheng, let alone in the markets here in the capital."

Bian Guanyue scratched her head. "Oh, is that so."

Chen Guiliang encouraged her, "It's already very delicious. It's perfectly normal for the taste to be slightly different."

The annual yield of Qixing peppers was too low. Even in local restaurants in Longdu, they might be substituted with Chaotian peppers.

Millet peppers were the lowest quality and cheapest option. They were neither spicy enough nor fragrant enough.

Perhaps because he had never eaten well as a child, Chen Guiliang became particularly particular about food after his financial situation improved in middle age. Before his rebirth, his palate had become increasingly discerning.

Of course, he could also make do with simple fare.

Bian Guanyue smiled. "Next time I go home, I'll bring some Qixing peppers back."

"No need to go to such trouble. Millet peppers are just a little lacking in aroma. I don't really care about the spiciness," Chen Guiliang said.

"It's no trouble, I'll just bring some along," Bian Guanyue said. "From now on, let's not hire a cook. The food we make ourselves tastes better."

This silly girl was already planning their life after marriage.

Her incomplete family since childhood had always been a lingering regret in her heart, so she wanted to create a perfect family of her own.

Watching Chen Guiliang eat the fish, Bian Guanyue continued, "I also want to learn how to make pickled vegetables. They're not easy to buy in the capital, and the flavor isn't very authentic. I heard they also grow mustard greens in the north, so the ingredients for pickled mustard greens should be easy to get."

To prevent her from making a mistake, Chen Guiliang could only remind her, "The variety of mustard greens in the north is different. It's a root mustard, with a mustard tuber. The pickled mustard greens in Sichuan are made with leaf mustard, which doesn't have a tuber. If you use northern mustard greens to make pickled mustard greens, you might as well use napa cabbage instead."

"Is that so? There's so much to learn about making pickled mustard greens." Bian Guanyue felt there was a lot she needed to learn.

After lunch, the two of them washed the dishes together and went back to the living room to watch TV.

Chen Guiliang leaned back on the sofa.

Bian Guanyue became more and more relaxed, her posture growing increasingly casual. She lay sideways on the sofa, her head resting on Chen Guiliang's thigh. She felt very relaxed watching TV like this.

"When I was little, I liked to rest my head on my grandmothers' laps and watch TV like this," Bian Guanyue said. "But they both said it wasn't good for me, that I'd become nearsighted if I watched for too long."

Chen Guiliang patted her head. "It's fine. You can lie however you want in the future."

"Hee hee." Bian Guanyue giggled.

There was nothing good on TV, so they were watching a disc today.

When Bian Guanyue had decorated the house, she had bought quite a few DVDs, both legitimate and pirated.

The reason she bought pirated discs despite having money was that the legitimate ones were mostly new releases, with a very limited selection of content. Pirated discs, on the other hand, offered a much wider variety, with all sorts of films from both home and abroad.

"This movie is so boring," Bian Guanyue said, watching a shoddily made old Hong Kong film.

Chen Guiliang asked, "How about we watch a horror movie?"

"No way. Things like 'The Ring' and 'Ju-On' are terrifying," Bian Guanyue objected.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Have you seen 'A Wicked Ghost'?"

Bian Guanyue said, "I think I've heard people mention it. It's a very famous film."

Chen Guiliang said, "It's a horror-comedy, similar to 'Mr. Vampire'."

"That's acceptable. I've seen 'Mr. Vampire'," Bian Guanyue said, then added with suspicion, "But why do I remember 'A Wicked Ghost' being very scary?"

"It's not that scary. There are only one or two really frightening scenes."

"Then let's watch it."

Half an hour later...

"Ah!"

Bian Guanyue shrieked and shrank into Chen Guiliang's arms, her eyes squeezed shut. "Turn off the TV, quick!"

Chen Guiliang said, "There's a twist. This is all just their imagination. If you don't believe me, just watch till the end."

Bian Guanyue's curiosity got the better of her and she opened her eyes again.

By the end of the movie, Chen Guiliang's arm had several new rows of teeth marks.

Bitten by an angry Bian Guanyue.

She was so angry she bit him as if she wanted to kill him. Like a dog.

The following weekend, the director of the Palace Museum personally led a team of photographers to give a commentary on some of the artifacts.

Talking about the artifacts was secondary; the main focus was on telling the stories behind them. That was what netizens were interested in.

Xiaonei Net did not participate in the course design or production, merely sending people over for a live text and photo broadcast.

This "Cyber Open Class" that Chen Guiliang was involved in was part of the "Voice of Civilization" online exhibition plan.

And "Voice of Civilization" was, in turn, part of the effort to clean up the internet.

Running concurrently was a campaign to crack down on online pornography and illegal publications.

One to promote good, one to punish evil, a two-pronged approach.

This kind of event had been held once before, last spring, but at that time it was limited to radio stations nationwide (including campus radio stations).

This year, People's Daily Online took the lead in participating, and Xiaonei Net immediately followed suit.

The guiding units included departments like the Communist Youth League, the State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television, the State Council Information Office, and the Central Civilization Commission. Websites from all over the country joined in one after another. Each had its own activities and methods, but all were actively cooperating with this initiative.

Chen Guiliang had just gotten involved a bit earlier; the other websites weren't fools. It was a chance to both curry favor with the relevant departments and boost their website's popularity, so of course they would go all out.

What was even more amusing was that Qianlong Net, together with 12 major websites in the Beijing area, formed a "Beijing Cyber Open Class" alliance.

Besides Xiaonei Net and Hainei Net, Sohu and Sina also joined.

Sina was in the process of forming an anti-Sohu alliance for Olympic coverage, and yet here they were, forming another alliance with Sohu to run the Cyber Open Class...

Chen Guiliang was amused by them.

There were many similar alliances. NetEase had also formed an alliance to host a "Cyber Open Class."

When Chen Guiliang proposed to promote and explain the history and artifacts of the Palace Museum, the other website alliances followed suit. Some promoted Yuelu Academy, some promoted Mazu culture, some promoted the six ancient capitals... in any case, they all dug into history and culture.

Coincidentally, the show "Lecture Room" had been a huge hit over the past two years, and professors like Yi, Yan, and Yu were in high demand. Major websites all sent out invitations, seeking to collaborate with them on lectures, which attracted a lot of attention.

Not long after the leaders from the Central Civilization Commission finished their inspection, a leader from the Communist Youth League also came to ByteDance.

"I hear that over half of all undergraduate, junior college, and postgraduate students in the country have registered accounts on Xiaonei Net?" the Youth League leader asked as they walked.

Chen Guiliang said, "At the start of the fall semester last year, it was close to 50%. Now it's estimated to be over 50%. This figure far exceeds the percentage of university students who own a computer."

The Youth League leader nodded. "With so many university student users, Xiaonei Net should place more emphasis on positive promotion."

Chen Guiliang led the leader and his entourage to a computer and went through the activities Xiaonei Net had hosted over the past two or three years.

Things like the campus belle contest were best left unmentioned.

What Chen Guiliang was showcasing at this moment were all positive and uplifting activities.

He also emphasized the three-line poetry contest: "Ever since the spring of the year after Xiaonei Net was founded, we have held a three-line poetry contest. It caused a huge sensation at the time, and was imitated by various sectors across the country. Now it's held every spring. It started with three-line love poems, but now the content of the poems has expanded to cover all aspects."

The award-winning three-line poems from previous years were pulled up by Chen Guiliang.

The Youth League leader took a look and saw that they were indeed all positive and uplifting poetic works. Even the love poems could be interpreted as odes to love.

The leader nodded repeatedly as he looked. "This event is very well run."

After inspecting for a full 40 minutes, the leader finally brought up specific cooperation.

In the future, any national activities guided, initiated, or hosted by the Youth League that were related to schools and students could be handed over to Xiaonei Net for online organization.

For example, the "National University Student Extracurricular Academic Science and Technology Works Competition," hosted in rotation by major universities across the country, would be jointly organized online by Xiaonei Net and other educational websites.

Xiaonei Net could also participate in the selection and reporting of events like the "Ten Outstanding Young Persons of China." Outstanding youths selected by Xiaonei Net could even receive a nomination spot, representing the student body to compete for the award.

For the past two or three years, the Youth League had been cooperating with Zhanzuo Net, because its founder had connections.

But Zhanzuo Net officially shut down last fall, and now Xiaonei Net was once again the dominant player. The Youth League had to choose a time to bring Xiaonei Net over to its side.

After seeing the leaders off, Chen Guiliang gathered his team for a meeting.

He briefly explained what had happened today. "We'll be organizing so many official events from now on. It won't be enough to just hire more staff, but relying solely on hiring more staff is also not the answer. Xiaonei Net is an SNS website; it mainly relies on users to generate content. Therefore, organizing these official events will still primarily depend on the students themselves..."

"We need to actively get in touch with student organizations and clubs. We should absorb the student union and club cadres from across the country as our collaborators. When there are activities, they can organize them. When there's news, they can disseminate it. When there are stories, they can report them..."

The employees in the meeting all laughed. It basically meant getting students to do free labor.

But the student union and club cadres would definitely be willing, and very proactive at that, because they needed to earn merits, win awards, and embellish their resumes.

Even without cooperating with Xiaonei Net, they would have to do those things anyway. And choosing to cooperate with Xiaonei Net would sometimes make their work even more convenient. At the very least, it would be helpful for publicity and organizing activities.

Ao Yanchen reminded him, "We shouldn't be like Zhanzuo Net, heavily publicizing our cooperative relationship with the Youth League and school authorities. We should also try to downplay our cooperation with the student unions of various schools. While it might sound more authoritative, it could actually offend ordinary students."

Xie Yang agreed, "That's right. Xiaonei Net is an online community for all students. We shouldn't mix in any official forces. Even if we do, we should try our best to downplay it. We need to let students have fun on Xiaonei Net, to let them feel completely uninhibited."

Chen Guiliang expressed his agreement. "Your points are very valid. Xiaonei Net is a platform for student interaction, not a place for relaying official decrees. The users are the foundation of our survival; cooperating with the Youth League is at best just the icing on the cake. Right after Zhanzuo Net was founded, it had an exclusive online partnership with the Youth League and China Youth Daily, but they already announced their closure last year."

The others also spoke their minds, jointly discussing how to handle the various official collaborations in the future.

Xiaonei Net already had a dedicated team for event planning. Now they would have to recruit a few more people. It would be best to directly hire recent graduates with experience in student unions or clubs.
